description: Procedural visual execution, authored background replacement, entity recognizability, HUD hierarchy, and mobile-safe visual refinement extracted from the clone unified-visual stage.

skills.title: Build the focal identity first
skills.intent: Make the protagonist or primary play identity the clearest embodiment of the remix world.
required_actions: Create or refine a focal actor, object, or branded piece family with distinctive silhouette, palette, and motif logic.
Derive enemies, collectibles, hazards, UI accents, and environment styling from that focal identity.
Keep the result readable and recognizable even in thumbnails.
acceptance_bar: The game looks intentionally remixed rather than lightly recolored.
Entities and UI belong to the same world grammar.

skills.title: Implement a reusable procedural art library
skills.intent: Favor reusable CSS/SVG/Canvas/DOM primitives over asset-led patchwork.
required_actions: Build reusable helpers for characters, hazards, rewards, particles, props, icons, and background motifs.
Prefer CSS variables, pseudo-elements, inline SVG, generated DOM shapes, canvas helpers, and lightweight motion systems.
Keep the implementation compatible with a simple HTML workspace.
acceptance_bar: The visual system can be extended without inventing new one-off styles.
Most identity-carrying visuals are code-native rather than pasted assets.

skills.title: Make the background an authored animated world layer
skills.intent: Turn the scene into a motion-graphic, theme-specific foundation instead of wallpaper.
required_actions: Create layered backgrounds with ambient motion, semantic motifs, and safe depth/parallax when useful.
Support progress/state-reactive changes while keeping foreground readability protected.
Ensure background animation never hides controls or gameplay-critical entities.
acceptance_bar: The scene feels authored and animated.
Background work supports the world without stealing gameplay attention.
failure_modes_prevented: Background layers with no connection to the remix premise

skills.title: Replace or demote dominant stock scenes
skills.intent: Reject unchanged stock backgrounds as the main playfield identity.
required_actions: Inspect real render paths, including image-backed scene layers and canvas draw calls.
Remove, transform, or strongly demote cheap stock scenes until they are no longer the dominant layer.
Do not count particles, overlays, or tint as a replacement by themselves.
acceptance_bar: The authored world owns the playfield.
Remaining image assets, if any, are subordinate rather than dominant.
failure_modes_prevented: Stock-scene ownership surviving under decorative garnish
False sense of completion from wrapper styling
Background drift away from the intended world

skills.title: Carry progression into scene evolution
skills.intent: Reflect escalation through level-reactive motifs, palette shifts, atmosphere, and world-state changes.
required_actions: Use safe hooks such as score, phase, labels, or existing state surfaces to show progression when possible.
Vary background states, motif density, particles, and lighting without implying new mechanics.
Keep all escalation readable on mobile.
acceptance_bar: Visual escalation matches the planned progression semantics.
Adjacent progression states are visibly distinct but still coherent.
failure_modes_prevented: Random scene changes unrelated to difficulty

skills.title: Refine visually without breaking HUD composition
skills.intent: Restyle and clarify the interface while preserving layouts that already work.
required_actions: Restyle before rearranging.
Keep critical buttons, modals, control zones, and overlays visible and tappable.
Compact and unclutter rather than expanding decorative chrome.
acceptance_bar: UI looks more authored and readable without shrinking playable space.
Mobile action paths remain intact.
failure_modes_prevented: HUD bulk that eats gameplay area

skills.title: Use browser-native techniques and safe libraries only when justified
skills.intent: Guide implementation toward HTML/CSS/JS-safe procedural techniques instead of fragile build-tool assumptions.
required_actions: Prefer CSS, SVG, Canvas, vanilla JS, and inline assets over bundler-dependent systems.
Use CDN libraries only for clear, bounded wins.
Map genre/style needs into practical browser-native techniques.
acceptance_bar: The visual system works in a simple HTML workspace.
Dependencies remain lightweight and explainable.
failure_modes_prevented: Bundler-only solutions in a plain HTML environment
Visual implementation that is hard to debug or repair

skills.title: Judge the visual result like a screenshot reviewer
skills.intent: Require a visual sanity pass before handing off to aggressive runtime QA.
required_actions: Check prompt alignment, focal identity strength, procedural design-system quality, cohesion, and mobile safety.
Fix obvious safe misses inside the visual phase rather than deferring everything to final repair.
Leave the final runtime repair phase focused on blockers, not basic art-direction misses.
acceptance_bar: The game already looks intentionally remixed before final repair.
Final QA can focus on real runtime defects.
failure_modes_prevented: Final QA trying to invent visual identity too late
Weak focal identity surviving the main art phase

skills.title: Map visual genres into concrete browser-native techniques
skills.intent: Preserve the high-value procedural graphics playbook instead of reducing it to vague 'visual polish' language.
required_actions: Translate fantasy, sci-fi, cute, horror, mythic, or hand-drawn goals into concrete CSS/SVG/Canvas/DOM motif strategies.
Choose whether the problem is better solved with CSS-first styling, SVG structure, Canvas atmospherics, or a tiny safe library.
Use technique choices to support the authored world and focal identity rather than generic decoration.
acceptance_bar: The visual system is buildable with specific browser-native methods.
Implementation choices are explainable rather than mystical.
failure_modes_prevented: Losing concrete implementation value during catalogization
Picking arbitrary visual techniques with no relation to genre or world
Procedural guidance collapsing into generic art-direction prose

skills.title: Carry forward visual anti-patterns and safety guardrails
skills.intent: Make sure strong visual ambition does not reintroduce fragile layouts, stock-scene ownership, or usability damage.
required_actions: Reject decorative bulk, wrapper-heavy systems, and overlays that swallow taps or hide controls.
Preserve stable HUD geometry when it already works.
Prefer restraint, coherence, and readable escalation over clutter, spectacle, or fragile flourish.
acceptance_bar: Visual ambition remains compatible with mobile actionability and repairability.
The art pass leaves behind fewer risks for final QA.
